analysis.title: Credit Crunch Imminent: Hyperscalers Blow Past Full-Year Debt Forecast As AI Bond Concessions Soar
key_insights: Since Oct 29 there have been five hyperscaler bond deals totaling $67B, taking Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle year-to-date global debt issuance to $296B against Goldman's full-year 2026 forecast of $250B.
Goldman's earlier Tuesday note counted three deals worth $41.7B and a YTD total of $271B. Two more deals added about $25B in two days.
Goldman attributes the overshoot to negative hyperscaler free cash flow in 3Q26, as capex outruns operating cash flow, and to a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply per company commentary.

YTD issuance equals 36% of 2026 hyperscaler capex, above the 33% debt-funded share Goldman initially assumed. Goldman sees scope for more pull-forward over the next few quarters, with uneven market access depending on market tone.

For 2027 Goldman still assumes 35% of hyperscaler capex is debt financed, about $440B of direct hyperscaler issuance, plus about $300B of project finance split between IG and HY. The author treats $440B as a floor.

Goldman sees risks to its spread forecasts as firmly tilted toward more widening between now and early December. It expects a modest overshoot of the March 2026 USD peaks (93bp IG, 335bp HY). As of the Nov 4 close, USD IG was 89bp and HY 324bp.
Goldman's EUR downside scenario uses April 2025 levels (128bp IG, 446bp HY). Its year-end targets are modestly tighter than current levels, reflecting the usual late-December supply lull.
Excess returns over Treasuries this year are 0.1% for USD IG, 0.0% for USD HY and -1.0% for EUR HY. Goldman recently moved from preferring IG over HY to preferring BBBs over As and AAs.
Goldman tracks $687B of global AI-related debt issuance in 2026 as of Nov 4 across IG, HY and leveraged loans. Hyperscalers are 43% of it. IG accounts for $568B and leveraged finance $119B.

In leveraged finance, data center and chip project financings are the two largest buckets, roughly $37B each across USD HY and USD leveraged loans. Goldman expects investors to be more selective on AI credit exposure and price.
AI deals are about 22% of USD IG gross supply and close to 20% in GBP, but under 8% in EUR IG, which Goldman says leaves room for euro AI issuance to grow.
There have been 27 USD IG deals of $10B or more this year, totaling $501B, about 2.5 times the prior record of about $200B. 14 of the 27, 66% of the dollar value (about $330B), were AI-related.
The average new issue concession on AI deals in November is about 18bp, versus under 7bp for non-AI deals and about 8bp for AI deals since the start of 2025.

Goldman tallies $1.7T of lease commitments, over 75% on leases not yet commenced, and $1.9T of other unconditional purchase commitments, $685B of it due by year-end 2027. Contingent backstop obligations are excluded.

The author's rebuild of Morgan Stanley's tally puts off-balance-sheet obligations across hyperscalers, Nvidia, Broadcom and SpaceX at $4.1T, up $1T in 90 days. Anthropic has $895B of committed spend per its S-1.
Goldman names delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments as the key risks to more debt issuance. Faster monetization would mean less.

Rating agency actions: Moody's said on Sept 22 that hyperscaler aggregate commitments rose eight-fold since 2023 to $2.8T. S&P warned on Oct 15 of a narrowing margin for error and cut outlooks on Broadcom and Meta in late October over off-balance-sheet obligations.
Goldman says evidence of monetization by 2028 is key to ratings. It judges multi-notch downgrades unlikely to cut off market access, comparing the path to Pharma's slow ratings drift a decade ago.

Goldman economists expect the midterm results to leave federal data center and AI regulation unchanged. Local data center moratoria could affect about 45% of planned US capacity, with Texas about 25%, and are expected to be short-lived.

Goldman says the HY primary market may be in a price discovery phase, with focus on project finance structures and offtaker quality. It sees macro-driven widening as offering attractive entry points for well-underwritten deals.

Goldman's fallback if syndicated markets choke is private capital: $17T of private markets per Preqin, $4.6T of dry powder, and more than $225B of data center financings since early 2025 excluding GPU and chip-collateralized deals. The author notes private credit defaults just hit a record.
The author expects the spread overshoot to be larger than modest and doubts the market will absorb another $67B week at 18bp concessions after the worst tech day since Covid.

market_movers.rationale: Microsoft issued its first dollar bond since 2017, a $25B-plus jumbo deal.
Oracle used its entire four-year capital-raising cap in a single morning, five days after announcing it.

S&P cut Meta's outlook in late October over leasing-driven leverage. Meta also tapped shareholders for up to $95B and its SEC filing says timing matters to secure capital before competitors saturate funding options.
S&P cut Broadcom's outlook in late October, citing residual value support on its AI compute contracts.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman moved from preferring IG over HY to preferring BBBs over As and AAs, and sees risks to spreads tilted toward widening until early December.
The author argues credit was the last asset class giving the AI trade the benefit of the doubt, and that supply, concessions and off-balance-sheet commitments are eroding it.

earnings_insights: Hyperscalers as a group reported negative free cash flow in 3Q26 (the author cites a prior piece putting the burn at $31B), as capex now outruns cash from operations.

risk_factors: Delayed AI monetization and growth in purchase commitments drive more debt issuance.
Supply saturation: huge jumbo deals at wide concessions reprice secondary spreads wider.
Off-balance-sheet obligations ($1.7T leases, $1.9T purchase commitments) eventually need funding by bonds, loans or equity.
Rating agency pressure from contingent guarantees and novel off-balance-sheet financing.
Local data center moratoria potentially affecting about 45% of planned US capacity.
Private credit, the fallback funder, just recorded record defaults.
HY project finance repricing and offtaker quality concerns.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and the SOX 12% on Thursday, the worst day for tech since Covid.
USD IG and HY spreads were 4bp and 11bp from their March 2026 peaks as of the Nov 4 close, before Thursday's selloff.
AI deals' November average new issue concession is about 18bp versus under 7bp for non-AI deals, which reprices secondary curves wider.
Asset allocators hold AI exposure across equities, syndicated credit and private markets at once, which the author reads as one trade owned three times.
geopolitical: Goldman economists expect Tuesday's midterm results to leave federal data center and AI regulation unchanged, with Democratic state and local wins likely to bring short-term data center moratoria.
The report mentions France's bond market stress as a concern for European IG investors.
cross_bank_references: Barclays drew a similar line between haves and have-nots in 'War Of Attrition'.

Goldman's $3.6T off-balance-sheet total is described as the conservative version versus Morgan Stanley's.

tension_points.theme: AI debt supply vs credit spreads
tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's base case is that the usual December supply lull bails out its year-end spread targets, which are modestly tighter than current levels. Goldman also says macro-driven widening offers attractive entry points for well-underwritten deals, and multi-notch downgrades are unlikely to cut off market access.
tension_points.bear_case: The author expects the overshoot of the March wides to be more than modest. Supply is running ahead of forecast, AI concessions are 18bp versus under 7bp for non-AI, off-balance-sheet commitments are in the trillions, and excess returns are about zero.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster AI monetization would mean less debt issuance, though Goldman calls that a 2028 story at best.

tension_points.theme: Private credit as AI funding backstop
tension_points.bull_case: Private markets hold $4.6T of dry powder and have done more than $225B of data center financings since early 2025, offering certainty of execution for large bespoke deals.
tension_points.bear_case: Private credit defaults just hit a record, which the author says makes it a peculiar lender of last resort.
